title: Standard Chartered puts Play On centre stage to help more girls stay in sport
article_text:
- Liverpool FC Men and Women replaced Standard Chartereds front-of-shirt logo with Play On, putting the issue of girls dropping out of sport in front of millions of fans.

- All proceeds from this years Perfect Match campaign will go to LFC Foundation to support programmes helping girls stay in sport.

- Standard Chartered convened organisations across the sporting ecosystem in Anfield, including UN Women, LFC and LFC Foundation, to help drive greater collective action on this issue.

Standard Chartered and Liverpool Football Club (LFC) have once again put Play On centre stage, using one of the most visible sponsorship assets in world sport to focus attention on helping more girls stay in sport.

The Play On message replaced Standard Chartereds usual branding on the front of the players shirts, with the LFCs Womens team wearing the Play On logo against Chelsea WFC on 21 November, followed by the Mens team against Manchester United FC at Anfield on 22 November.

Ahead of both fixtures, a giant 25m x 23m Play On shirt was displayed on the pitch at St Helens and Anfield Stadiums, reinforcing the campaigns call to help girls stay in sport.

The limited-edition match shirts are now being signed and auctioned, with proceeds from this years campaign going to LFC Foundation, supporting programmes designed to break down barriers and help more girls participate in sport.

Standard Chartered also convened organisations and individuals working across sport, business and civil society at Anfield to discuss how greater collective action can help address the barriers girls face. Guests included representatives from UN Women, the International Working Group on Women and Sport, LFC and LFC Foundation.

This builds on Standard Chartereds longer-term ambition for Play On, connecting organisations with different capabilities, from funding and programme delivery to policy expertise, communications reach and access to communities, to explore how they can work together more effectively to keep girls in sport.

Erica Kerner, Global Head of Brand Partnerships and Sponsorships, Standard Chartered, said: Sport gives girls so much more than the opportunity to play. It can build confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership skills that can open doors throughout their lives. Yet girls still drop out of sport at twice the rate of boys by the age of 14. Through Play On, were leveraging the power and reach of our partnership with LFC to shine a light on this issue, connecting brands and organisations to create more opportunities for girls to fulfil their potential on and beyond the pitch.

Kate Theobald, SVP of Global Partnerships at Liverpool FC, said: Our long-standing partnership with Standard Chartered has always been about more than football, and Play On is a great example of how we can work together to make a meaningful difference. Since launching the initiative in 2023, weve continued to build on its impact, using the clubs global reach and the strength of our partnership to raise awareness of the barriers girls face in sport and encourage positive change.

Were incredibly proud of what weve achieved together through Play On over the years, and particularly pleased that this years campaign will directly support LFC Foundation and its work to create more opportunities for girls to stay involved in sport. Its another important step in our shared commitment to making a lasting difference.

Play On was launched by Standard Chartered and LFC in 2023 to help more girls stay in sport and benefit from the skills, confidence and opportunities it can create throughout their lives.

The joint Standard Chartered and LFC Play On initiative aims to help girls stay in sport as it builds confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership  skills that can lead to opportunities in education, employment and wider life.

Play On was launched in 2023 to support the Banks Lifting Participation Stand and ambitions. To-date, it has mainly been campaign-based, aiming to raise awareness of the following:

- Twice as many girls than boys drop out of sports by age 14.

- 94 per cent of women in C-suite roles played sport as girls.

- 74 per cent of executive women believe a background in sport can help accelerate a womans career.

Tactically, we teamed up with LFC Academy and Foundation coaches to deliver our bespoke Play On Train the Trainer programme through our community partners in Kenya and South Africa: 69 local coaches were upskilled through the training, who went on to train more than 10,500 girls over the following year.

We are a leading international banking group, with a presence in 55 of the worlds most dynamic markets. Our purpose is to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, and our heritage and values are expressed in our brand promise, here for good.

Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London and Hong Kong stock exchanges.

title: Amex Stadium will host 2035 Women's World Cup matches
article_text:
Brighton's Amex Stadium could host matches at the 2035 Women's World Cup, after a successful bid from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

The ground was among 19 venues listed as possible host stadiums at a FIFA meeting yesterday after football’s governing body gave its approval to the plans.

The 104-match tournament will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the UK since 1966.

Brighton and Hove City Council previously expressed a desire to become one of the host cities for the tournament in late 2025, highlighting potential benefits including tourism and global media exposure.

The Amex, which can seat more than 32,000 supporters, previously played host to several matches at the 2022 Women's Euros, including two involving England.

Among the other English venues for the 2035 tournament are Wembley, Villa Park, Bristol's Ashton Gate and Newcastle's St James' Park.

title: LPGA to replace Japan Classic with Konami-backed event
article_text:
Women’s golf’s top-tier LPGA has announced that its tournament in Japan will be revamped next year with a larger prize purse and title sponsorship from Japanese video game developer Konami.

The Konami Championship replaces the LPGA’s Toto Japan Classic in 2027 and will be held over four days, from November 4 to 7, at Taiheiyo Club’s Minori Course in Omitama, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The tournament will feature 78 players – 43 from the LPGA Tour and 35 from the Japan Ladies Professional Golf Association (JLPGA) Tour.

Significantly, the new tournament will have an increased purse of $3 million, up from the $2.1 million offered at the Japan Classic, making it one of the highest-paying women’s golf tournaments held in Japan.

Alongside prize money of $450,000, the winner will receive a two-year LPGA Tour card for the following year.

Kimihiko Higashio, chief executive of Konami Group Corporation, said: “This tournament has grown steadily since 1973 as the only official LPGA Tour event held in Japan.

“We are honored to participate as the host and title sponsor of a tournament with a long history and tradition. Konami Group is exploring new ways to realize our corporate purpose of ‘Experience Well-being Moments’ through games, sports, and various entertainment fields.”

The announcement comes as the LPGA continues to consolidate its 2027 calendar, having unveiled a revamp for its Championship tournament in the UK, with the LPGA co-sanctioning the event with the Ladies European Tour (LET), and Golf Saudi providing financial backing.

The Championship, played between July 19 and 25, appears to be taking the place of the Women’s Scottish Open, which is reportedly no longer on the LPGA schedule, and will have an overall prize purse of $4 million.

The tour’s ongoing 2026 season features 33 events across 13 countries and a record total prize purse of over $132 million.

For Konami, the new title sponsorship adds to its visibility within sport, having signed up this year as a global sponsor to this year’s 2026 World Baseball Classic (WBC) national teams competition.

The Japanese developer has an extensive soccer portfolio, which includes a licensing deal with the French Football Federation national body, major European clubs such as AC Milan, Arsenal, Barcelona, Borussia Dortmund, Inter Milan, and Manchester United, as well as the top-flight J.League domestically.

title: More Details Emerge on NASCAR Sponsor’s Fraud as Founder Allegedly Diverted $11M to Racing Team
article_text:
EssentiallySports is the home for the underserved fan, delivering storytelling that goes beyond the headlines. As a media platform, we combine deep audience insights with cultural trends, to meet fandom where it lives and where it goes next. Founded in 2014, EssentiallySports now engages with an audience of over 30m+ American sports fan on its website and 1m+ readers on its newsletters daily.

The allegations surrounding Droplight founder Phillip Williams have already sent shockwaves through NASCAR and IndyCar, with the company’s sponsorship ties drawing fresh scrutiny after his arrest in an alleged $600 million investment fraud. But newly unsealed regulatory complaints have revealed just how far the alleged misuse of investor money may have reached into motorsports. One filing points to more than $11 million spent on an unnamed racing team, while another identifies a separate $500,000 sponsorship expense. Neither recipient is named.

As reported by Bob Pockrass on X, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s complaint against Williams, Devin Johnson and several related companies alleges that Williams used more than $11 million in misappropriated investor funds for an “apparent auto racing team.” The filing does not identify the recipient, leaving an important question unanswered as the case unfolds. It does, however, add a significant new detail to the scandal surrounding Droplight, the company Williams co-founded and used to build a growing presence in American sports sponsorship.

The CFTC alleges that Williams, including through his company KMAP, diverted investor money for personal spending and transfers to businesses he owned or controlled. The alleged racing expenditure appears alongside millions of dollars in other transactions, including more than $3.2 million for apparent real estate purchases, $3 million to an apparent bare-knuckle fighting promoter, and over $1.8 million for luxury car garage space. These are allegations in a civil complaint, not findings established at trial.

The same filing identifies another motorsports-related expense involving Williams’ co-founder, Devin Johnson. According to the CFTC, Johnson used $500,000 in investor funds for an “apparent auto racing sponsorship.” That payment is separate from the more than $11 million attributed to Williams, and the complaint does not name the sponsorship recipient either. IndyStar reported that Johnson’s SalesAi business sponsored Dreyer & Reinbold Racing’s No. 24 entry in the past two Indianapolis 500s, although Insvt served as the primary sponsor. The regulatory filing itself does not identify the team, so the reported sponsorship connection should not be mistaken for an explicit allegation against the racing organization.

The latest filings also shed light on Droplight’s own financial connection to the alleged scheme. In its complaint, the Securities and Exchange Commission says the Williams-controlled entity received $31 million sourced from KMAP, which the regulator alleges was fraudulently obtained from Backward Hat investors. The SEC named Droplight as a relief defendant, a legal designation used when a party is alleged to have received proceeds or property connected to wrongdoing but is not accused of participating in the underlying fraud. The complaint states that Droplight has no legitimate claim to those funds.

That distinction is important because Droplight had become a visible name in motorsports sponsorship. The company backed Louis Foster’s No. 45 IndyCar entry at Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing and was also connected to Freedom Racing in the NASCAR Truck Series. IndyStar reported that Droplight sponsored the RLL entry beginning at the 2025 Indianapolis 500 and that the company was no longer listed among the team’s partners after the allegations became public. RLL told the publication it was aware of the allegations and was conducting a fact-finding process. Neither RLL nor Foster is named as a participant in the alleged fraud in the SEC or CFTC complaints.

The money at the center of the case was allegedly raised through Backward Hat Capital, an investment operation founded by Williams and Johnson. The SEC says the enterprise raised approximately $560 million from more than 2,000 investors by promoting an AI-driven foreign-exchange strategy that purportedly generated returns of at least 6% every month. The CFTC puts the amount at more than $556 million from at least 2,100 participants, while federal prosecutors have described the broader alleged scheme as involving more than $600 million. The figures come from different proceedings and should not be treated as identical totals.

According to the SEC, the promised trading strategy involved little or no actual foreign-exchange trading. More than $250 million allegedly went toward Ponzi-like payments to earlier investors, while more than $220 million was transferred to the founders or their entities. The regulator also alleges that the operation relied on false financial reports to reassure investors about its performance. The CFTC similarly says investor funds were diverted for personal use and unrelated expenses rather than used as promised.

The fallout now extends beyond the two executives and the investment funds. Federal authorities have obtained emergency relief, including an asset freeze, and a temporary receiver has been appointed to take control of specified companies and assets. Williams and Johnson were arrested on November 18 and face federal criminal charges, while the SEC and CFTC proceedings are separate civil enforcement actions. The allegations have not been proven in court, and both men are presumed innocent.

For NASCAR and IndyCar, the immediate concern is the financial uncertainty surrounding a sponsor that had secured prominent racing partnerships. The filings do not establish that any team knowingly received misappropriated money or took part in the alleged scheme. But the newly disclosed figures raise serious questions about how much investor money may have flowed into motorsports through different channels, and what happens to sponsorship agreements when the source of that funding comes under federal scrutiny.

title: Women’s specific ball trial extended for second season of HSBC SVNS Series
article_text:
- World Rugby confirms extension of bespoke smaller, size 4.5 ball trial for women's sevens throughout the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS Series and Championship

The trial forms part of World Rugby's ongoing commitment to exploring innovations that support the continued development of women's rugby. Designed to assess whether a bespoke ball could enhance aspects of skill execution and overall playing experience, the initiative places player feedback and evidence-based evaluation at the centre of the decision-making process.

More than 130 elite women's sevens players and 18 coaches provided feedback on the bespoke 4.5 ball compared with the traditional size 5 ball, assessing key aspects of play including handling, kicking and set-piece performance. Initial feedback was encouraging, with positive sentiment outweighing negative sentiment by a ratio of 4:1.

The Sevens ball, which is a bespoke 4.5 size, has been specially designed in with Sevens performance in mind with an emphasis on aerodynamics for passing, grip for handling and a similar weight to the size 5 ball for familiarity. It also has a bespoke sweet spot for kicking that is not found on regular 4.5 balls.

The ball has also been trialed at the 15s game with player feedback from the WXV Global Series and Challenger currently being collected following the conclusion of the series at the end of October. A decision on next steps will be made by all stakeholders (players, unions and World Rugby) at the World Rugby Shape of the Game meeting which will be held at the beginning of 2027.

World Rugby Chief Player Welfare and Rugby Services Officer Mark Harrington said; “The initial findings from the first season of this trial are encouraging, both in terms of player feedback and what we're seeing in the performance data.

“Extending the trial for a second season will allow us to assess whether these positive trends are sustained over time, while continuing to gather valuable insights from players. It's important that we take a thorough, evidence-led approach to understanding the impact of the ball and ensuring that any decisions are informed by both player experience and performance data.

“With the LA 2028 Olympic Games on the horizon, we want to continue exploring opportunities to support innovation and performance in women's sevens. Ultimately, this is about giving the world's best players the best possible platform to showcase their skills on the global stage.”

Chief of Women’s Rugby Sally Horrox added: “We know that using a specific ball for the women’s game has generated considerable discussion, and we welcome that engagement. This trial was initiated following requests from unions and player representative bodies, and we’ve been clear from the outset that their feedback would be central to determining the next steps.

"What’s particularly encouraging is the positive response we’ve received from sevens players, alongside the early performance data. Extending the trial for a second season will allow us to build on these initial findings, gather further insights, and ensure that any future decisions are informed by robust evidence and the experiences of the players themselves.

title: Maincast Sport secures WTA broadcast rights in Ukraine
article_text:
Maincast Sport has acquired the rights to broadcast the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in Ukraine under a long-term agreement, bringing the world's leading women's professional tennis tour to Ukrainian audiences with dedicated Ukrainian-language coverage.

The agreement will give fans access to Ukrainian-language coverage of WTA tournaments throughout the 2027 season, as the Tour visits 26 countries and territories. From Brisbane and Auckland in January, the season will take in iconic destinations including Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Rome and Beijing, culminating in the season-ending FAGE WTA Finals in Charlotte, USA, in November.

The WTA Tour joins Maincast Sport’s portfolio of international sports properties including the NBA, Copa del Rey, MotoGP and NASCAR. Now with the WTA, the addition further strengthens Maincast Sport’s offering, bringing fans world-class women’s tennis and the opportunity to follow the Ukrainian players who consistently compete at the highest level.

The partnership includes: International WTA 1000 events, WTA 500 Events, WTA 250 Events, and the FAGE WTA Finals taking place in Charlotte (USA), where the season’s top eight singles players and doubles teams will compete.

“Tennis is one of the sports where Ukraine has genuine stars, and fans have followed every match our players have played for years. From 2027, matches featuring Elina Svitolina, Marta Kostyuk, Dayana Yastremska and other Ukrainian players will be available exclusively on Maincast Sport, alongside hundreds of matches from the world’s best players. We’re creating our own tennis shows, analysis and broadcasts with star guests. The WTA calendar runs almost all year round, so Maincast Sport viewers will get top-level tennis every week,,” said Vitalii Volochai, co-founder of Maincast.

“We’re delighted to partner with Maincast Sport to bring more women’s tennis to fans in Ukraine, where the sport already means so much. Ukrainian players continue to make an important impact on the global stage, and this agreement will give fans more opportunities to follow their favourite athletes and experience the excitement of the WTA Tour throughout the season,” said Marina Storti, CEO of WTA Ventures.

WTA Tour matches will be available to fans on the Maincast Sport TV channel and Maincast.tv platform.

title: Disney+ grows DACH portfolio with Bundesliga highlights sublicence from RTL
article_text:
Media giant Disney has sub-licensed a package of rights concerning the German Bundesliga elite soccer property from rights holder RTL Deutschland, expanding its sports portfolio across the DACH region.

The Disney+ OTT streaming service will now broadcast highlights packages for every Bundesliga and second-tier Bundesliga 2 game in the territories of Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein (the DACH region).

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

This agreement will begin on January 1, covering the second half of the current 2026-27 campaign, and run through the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons.

Coverage will be hosted in the ESPN content area on Disney+ services, at no extra cost to existing users.

Speaking on the deal, RTL Deutschland managing director of content Inga Leschek said: “The Walt Disney Company and RTL Deutschland have enjoyed a long-standing relationship in content licensing. We’re delighted to now strengthen that relationship in sports as well on Disney+, helping to further increase the visibility and reach of the leagues.”

Disney general manager for networks and sports for EMEA (Europe, the Middle East and Africa) Diego Londono added: “As ESPN on Disney+ continues to expand across Europe, bringing Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 highlights to customers in Germany marks another important milestone.

“This agreement gives fans a new way to experience the best moments from Germany’s top two football leagues and further strengthens our growing sports offering on Disney+.”

This follows the recent launch of ESPN as a content area on Disney+ to select markets across Europe, positioning the iconic US sports broadcasting brand as Disney’s key consumer sports arm.

In Germany in particular, the platform holds the rights to UEFA Women's Champions League soccer, Formula E motor racing, and more.

The wider lineup also features college sports such as the NCAA men's and women's basketball tournaments (March Madness), college football playoffs, and bowl games, as well as other sports rights in select markets, most recent of those being the NHL, and NBA basketball in 11 European markets.

title: Baller League launches international women’s competition
article_text:
Baller League has introduced a women’s competition as part of its new Nations Cup, creating an international six-a-side tournament for amateur female players across 16 countries and 64 cities.

The women’s tournament will run alongside a men’s competition, with both winning teams receiving equal $1m prizes. Teams will progress from city-level tournaments to national qualifiers before the 16 national champions compete at the international finals.

The format will allow amateur teams to enter without affiliation to a professional club, academy or agent. Registration is scheduled to open in March 2027, with the competition running from 26th June until the final weekend from 5th-7th November.

The introduction of the women’s tournament represents an expansion of Baller League’s existing six-a-side format. Founded in Germany in 2024, the competition has since established leagues in the UK and United States.

The equal prize allocation means a combined $2m will be awarded to the men’s and women’s champions. Baller League founder and CEO Felix Starck has described each $1m award as what the organisation believes to be the largest prize offered to amateur footballers, although that claim has not been independently verified.

For the UK, the Nations Cup will build on Baller League’s existing domestic presence and provide amateur women’s teams with a route from local competition to representing their country in an international tournament.

title: FIFA advances 2030 U.S. World Cup media rights bidding, Netflix in driver’s seat
article_text: FIFA has advanced its bidding process for U.S. media rights to the 2030 Men’s World Cup to a second round, with the world governing body “aiming to create a bidding war between Netflix and Fox Sports/Univision.” Sources said Netflix “submitted the largest bid before last week’s deadline and are now regarded as frontrunners,” with FIFA understood to have “invited second bids in an attempt to drive up the price.” Asking for a second bid is “not unusual in a media rights tender even when there is a clear leader in the first round,” which “appears to be the case in this instance.” Netflix is understood to have “initially trumped offers” from Amazon and the joint bid from Fox and Spanish-language broadcaster Univision. FIFA has sought between $1.5B and $2B for its 2030 U.S. broadcast deal after opting to sell English and Spanish-language rights together for the first time, which “would represent a significant raise” from the $485M and $600M it received for last summer’s tournament from Fox and Telemundo, respectively (London GUARDIAN, 11/23).

title: Shorts: Welsh Rugby Union, MATTA, Sport In Mind
article_text:
Isuzu UK has extended its partnership with the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) for a further two years, taking the relationship into its second decade.

Isuzu, which first partnered with the WRU in 2017, will continue as pick-up vehicle supplier, providing a fleet of 37 D-Max trucks to support the governing body’s work across Wales.

The vehicles help WRU coaches, development staff and community teams deliver activities throughout the country, transporting equipment and resources for grassroots programmes, development projects and community activations.

The WRU’s community membership for the 2026/27 season includes nearly 56,000 men and boys, 7,000 women and girls, 6,300 registered coaches and more than 1,100 registered match officials.

Tomos Grace, Chief Commercial Officer at the Welsh Rugby Union, said, “We are delighted to extend our partnership with Isuzu for a further two years and hugely appreciate the continued support they provide to Welsh rugby. The Isuzu D-Max fleet is an important part of our ability to deliver activities, right across Wales. This practical support enables our teams to get out into communities, work alongside our clubs and partners, and support Welsh rugby at every level of the game. We are grateful to Isuzu for their long-standing commitment and look forward to continuing our relationship over the next two years.”

George Wallis, Head of Marketing at Isuzu UK, said, “We applaud the work being done by the Welsh Rugby Union, and we’re proud to lend the Isuzu D-Max’s pulling power to an outreach programme that achieves so much in communities across Wales. In the spirit of the WRU, the Isuzu D-Max is a workhorse that keeps going to deliver the performance required, and we’re delighted to continue as part of the team for the years ahead.”

The D-Max range includes the UK’s first fully capable battery electric pick-up alongside a new 2.2 diesel engine.

English county cricket’s short-format competition, formerly the Vitality Blast, has been renamed the T20 Blast, with a new visual identity built around its status as the world’s original T20 competition.

The ECB worked with independent sports creative agency MATTA on the refresh, which uses ‘The Original T20’ as its creative platform. The positioning gives the competition a clear lane alongside The Hundred and gives counties a foundation to promote the format.

The competition staged the world’s first professional T20 match in June 2003 and will enter its 25th season in 2027. The new brand centres on county belonging and local rivalries, and gives counties the freedom to adopt their own colours and style over time. Restoring “T20” to the name is designed to make the competition easier for new fans to understand, from the opening Blast Off fixtures through Friday nights and the Knockouts to Finals Day.

The rebrand lands on the same day Gloucestershire unveiled the Bristol Lions as its new T20 identity for the men’s and women’s teams.

Matt Hunt, Executive Strategy Director at MATTA, said, “Breathing fresh life into the T20 Blast competition was an opportunity that we grabbed with both hands – to put the counties front and centre in telling their own stories from a platform of originality – a word that is at once both creative and authoritative. We wanted to reflect that in the proud, competitive, authentic and powerful nature of the competition.”

Cordelia Brown, Marketing Director at the ECB, said, “We are delighted with how the new T20 Blast brand expresses the unique nature of the tournament, flexible enough to allow individual county expression but strong enough to be readily and easily identifiable as the assured and definitive creator of the format – and are looking forward to working with the counties to help make this truly a season to remember.”

Fixtures for the 2027 season will be released on Wednesday 25th November.

The festival takes place from Friday 28th-Sunday 30th May 2027 at Chapel Gate, Bournemouth, and will welcome thousands of players and festival-goers for a weekend of sport, music and entertainment.

The partnership will raise awareness of the role sport and physical activity can play in supporting mental health and wellbeing. Sport In Mind will have a presence at the festival, engaging attendees and introducing its work to a wider audience. The Reading-based charity has supported more than 100,000 children, young people and adults through sport and physical activity.

Matt Hall, Managing Director of Bournemouth 7s Festival, said, “We’re incredibly proud to welcome Sport In Mind as our Official Charity Partner for 2027, especially as we celebrate our 20th anniversary. Sport has always been at the heart of Bournemouth 7s, but for us, it’s about so much more than what happens on the pitch. It’s about bringing people together and the positive impact being part of a team can have on people’s lives.“

“Sport In Mind does some fantastic work demonstrating just how powerful sport can be for mental health and wellbeing. It feels like a really natural partnership, and we’re looking forward to using our platform to help raise awareness of the important work they do.”

Phil Rose, Chair of Trustees at Sport In Mind, said, “We’re delighted to be joining Bournemouth 7s Festival as its Official Charity Partner for such a special anniversary year. We know first-hand the positive impact sport and physical activity can have on mental health, and we’re excited to work together to share that message with thousands of festival-goers. It’s a fantastic opportunity to celebrate the power of sport to bring people together and make a real difference.”

title: Roberts Travel Group joins Leicester City
article_text:
Leicestershire-based Roberts Travel Group has joined Leicester City as club partner and coach supplier until the end of the 2026/27 season.

The local operator will run the club’s away supporter coach travel, alongside a range of other transport and travel operations, including coaches for the boys’ and girls’ academies. Supporters will also see the brand across matchday and Fan Zone entertainment and on the club’s digital platforms.

The deal follows last week’s agreement with recruitment platform Bossjob, which became the club’s front-of-shirt partner for the rest of the season.

Russell Jones, Commercial Director at Leicester City, said, “We’re delighted to welcome Roberts Travel Group as an Official Partner and our Official Coach Supplier. It’s fantastic to have another successful local business join our Club as an Official Partner. Roberts provide such a valuable service to local people – from transporting thousands of children to school to providing unique holiday trips across the country.“

“For Leicester City, Roberts continue to provide coaches for our boys and girls academies, and our away coaches, helping fans get around the country to support the team. Thank you to the team at Roberts Travel Group for taking this next step by becoming an Official Partner. We’re really excited to see how we can continue to grow our partnership in the months and years ahead.”

Alex Niemczyk, Managing Director at Roberts Travel Group, said, “We’re incredibly proud to become an Official Partner and Official Coach Supplier of Leicester City. As a Leicestershire-based business, this partnership is particularly special to us, and we are delighted to be working alongside a club with such a strong connection to its local community.“

“At Roberts Travel Group, we understand just how important football is to fans, and we are committed to providing safe, reliable and comfortable travel experiences for supporters following their team. We look forward to building a successful partnership with Leicester City and playing our part in helping fans enjoy their matchday experience.”

Amazon becomes Invictus Games headline sponsor
article_text:
Amazon has become headline sponsor of the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, its biggest commitment to the Games to date, as preparations build for the tournament’s return to the UK.

The company will provide funding and support across technology, marketing and operational delivery, alongside employee volunteering and community engagement. The aim is to help the Games tell stories of recovery, resilience and achievement to audiences around the world.

Birmingham 2027 will be the third Invictus Games that Amazon has supported, following Düsseldorf in 2023 and Vancouver Whistler in 2025.

This news comes after Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 confirmed the continuation of its partnership with Ottobock, which will provide technical support for competitors during the Games in the UK, and named ITV as its exclusive UK broadcaster last week.

The Games take place at the NEC and Sandwell Aquatics Centre from 10th to 17th July 2027. Up to 550 competitors from 26 nations will take part across 12 adaptive sports, joined by 1,100 friends and family members, with more than 150,000 supporters expected. It will be the first time the Games have been held in the UK since the inaugural edition in London in 2014.

Birmingham was chosen for its long connection to the recovery and rehabilitation of the Armed Forces community. The city is home to Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham and the Royal Centre for Defence Medicine, where hundreds of British service personnel wounded in Iraq and Afghanistan were treated.

Helen Helliwell, CEO of Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, said, “I’ve seen first-hand Amazon’s commitment to supporting the Armed Forces community, creating career opportunities and providing vital support for serving personnel, veterans and their families. We’re delighted to have them as Headline Sponsor of Birmingham 2027 as their support will help us deliver an exceptional Games.”

Lisa Swan, General Manager of Birmingham Operations at Amazon, said, “Thousands of our colleagues call Birmingham and the West Midlands home, so it’s a proud moment to be part of bringing the Invictus Games into our region. As headline sponsor, we’re looking forward to giving something back to the communities that support us every day, and to playing our part in a Games that we hope will inspire people across the city and region.”

The partnership builds on Amazon’s wider support for the Armed Forces community. Through its Global Military Affairs team, it works with military organisations, charities and local communities to create careers, skills training and support for veterans, serving personnel, reservists and military families. In the UK, dedicated military recruiters help members of the military community find civilian roles, supported by career transition programmes and a paid military leave policy.

title: KSA intervenes on Champions League sponsorship
article_text:
The organisation blocked Inter Milan and Club Brugge's proposed shirt sponsorship.

The Dutch Gaming Authority (KSA) has stepped in to prevent two Champions League clubs from playing in the Netherlands with a gaming company as their shirt sponsor.

Betsson is the usual shirt sponsor for Inter Milan and Club Brugge, which does not have a licence for the Dutch market.

For the matches which are to be played in the Netherlands, the clubs offered to use the name Betsson.Foundation, as this is a non-profit oragnisation.

However, the KSA still objected on the grounds that it was "insufficiently distinctive from the gambling provider."

As a result, Inter Milan is set to play without a shirt sponsor and Club Brugge will simply use different text on their match shirts. Betsson declined to comment on the matter.

Alongside the KNVB, the largest sports organisation in the Netherlands, the KSA reiterated to foreign football clubs and associations that the Dutch rules on gambling advertising apply not only to Dutch clubs but also to foreign clubs playing matches in the Netherlands.

The KSA announced in October that the country's GGR had shrunk in 2025.

title: Host City 2026 to bring global event leaders to Glasgow to shape the future of major events
‘Our category felt dusty’: Why Strauss now spends a third of its marketing budget on sponsorship
article_text:
When German workwear brand Strauss concluded its long-running sponsorship of the country’s national soccer team at the end of 2025, it might have seemed peculiar timing.

The company had been a partner of the German Football Association (DFB) since 2010, and the relationship ended on the eve of a Fifa World Cup year – a major tournament where interest around Die Mannschaft would typically peak.

However, in September, a new deal with Uefa offered some insight into how Strauss’s sponsorship strategy is shifting.

Already a sponsor of the Europa League and Conference League club competitions, the company expanded its relationship with European soccer’s governing body to become its first-ever official referee partner, spanning men’s and women’s club and national team competitions, including the Champions League and the Euros.

Germany’s on-field performances might have dipped in recent years, but Henning Strauss, chief executive of the company founded by his grandfather Engelbert in 1948, says the DFB partnership was highly successful and that the two sides parted on good terms. The brand is now growing faster in markets like the UK than it is at home, meaning the focus has moved towards partnerships that help build relevance overseas.

“Correct,” says Strauss, when SportsPro asks whether the company feels it no longer needs to buy awareness in Germany, where it already has strong recognition and market penetration.

“It’s really time to shift that budget and make sure we achieve awareness and ultimately growth outside of our home market,” he adds. “The Europa League and the Conference League have [already] been extremely helpful, and that’s taken us to who we are today – strong in our home market, but that’s at the moment underperforming [compared to] all the other countries.”

The company’s partnership with Uefa includes logo placement on referee sleeves, as well as branding on video assistant referee (VAR) monitors and in the control room, offering significant media value during emotionally charged moments when television viewers are paying close attention to the decision of the match officials.

That said, it would be fair to say that referees aren’t universally loved by supporters, while VAR has courted its fair share of controversy since being adopted across European soccer. Strauss acknowledges that VAR decisions are a “very intense moment” where one set of fans will inevitably be unhappy. But the deal also creates narrative alignment with the company’s efforts to use sponsorship to spotlight the skill of those who typically go unrecognised.

“Well, it was something we talked about,” Strauss says, when asked whether the company considered the sponsorship a risk.

“But in that particular case, there’s also a story to tell. And Uefa, with us in the back, does a good job telling that story. And I think the referees need more respect, because that really is a very challenging task. So, they came up with the slogan ‘Lead when it’s Loud’, because that’s really what it’s about. I’ve spoken to some of the head referees, and they mentioned a lot of times they had difficulty falling asleep following matches.

“So they do need more respect and, you know, sort of an understanding.”

The Uefa refereeing deal is seen as part of the company’s wider efforts to expand its business outside of the German-speaking world. Key international territories include the UK, Australia and North America, which Strauss describes as the brand’s “biggest growth market at the moment by far”.

The company’s rapidly expanding sponsorship portfolio reflects those priorities. Since 2023, it has partnered with Major League Baseball (MLB), the Australian Football League (AFL), the Big Ten Conference and the National Football League (NFL) in Europe, as well as soccer clubs like Liverpool, Los Angeles FC and Nottingham Forest. The company is also an official partner of Uefa Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland – a deal exclusively revealed by SportsPro back in October – after sponsoring the 2024 edition in Germany. Outside of sport, there have even been workwear collaborations with Metallica and Mario Kart.

All told, Strauss says sponsorship now accounts for about a third of the company’s marketing budget, which he later clarified runs to a few hundred million euros, representing a sizeable investment for a family-owned business that most recently reported annual revenue of €1.4 billion (US$1.6 billion). Those partnerships, managed by a separate in-house team, are primarily seen as an “awareness builder”, while most of what’s left goes on digital performance marketing and direct sales.

That said, Strauss is keen to stress that the company doesn’t simply choose partnerships based on reach. When he joined the business in 2001, he encountered a category he felt was “very conservative” and “very dusty in many ways”. Sponsorship therefore plays a central role in his ambition to make the brand more aspirational, something he says has helped attract “excellent talent” in recent years.

From a quality perspective, the company wants its workwear products, like trousers, bibs, jackets and boots, to be viewed as the premium option for its core audience of tradespeople like roofers and electricians, whether they are sporting them in the workplace or when participating in lifestyle activities like skiing or hiking.

As a result, the company is prioritising partnerships that not only associate the business with top-tier sports properties, but also position it next to sponsors that are global premium brands. Through its Uefa partnerships for example, Strauss sits alongside the likes of Adidas, Coca-Cola and Mastercard.

“From an advertising and a brand point of view, [what sort of ecosystem we are part of] to me is extremely important,” Strauss says. “Our portfolio reflects who we are, but where we are going.

title: HSBC Race to Finals Complete
article_text:
Following the conclusion of the LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Sunday, the top eight qualifiers for the season-ending HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 are now locked in. The season finale, which is the most lucrative prize money tournament of the season, will be held in Hangzhou, China from 9-13 December 2026. Players will be competing for a share of the prize money pot of US$3.5 million.

The race in men’s singles had gone to the wire, with the final qualifying tournament (Hong Kong Open 2026), determining the fates of four players. A surprise loss for Koki Watanabe in the first round helped Chou Tien Chen, Lakshya Sen and Kunlavut Vitidsarn seal their spots.

France have a strong presence through world champion Alex Lanier and No.1 Christo Popov; the other qualifiers are Alwi Farhan, Victor Lai and Anders Antonsen.

World champion An Se Young is one title away from setting an all-time record of 12 titles in a season. An was the standout performer on the World Tour, followed by Akane Yamaguchi, Wang Zhi Yi, Chen Yu Fei, Tomoka Miyazaki and the resurgent Pusarla V Sindhu.

Ratchanok Intanon secured a record 11th qualification at the World Tour Finals with a semifinal placing in Hong Kong, and will be joined in Hangzhou by her compatriot Pornpawee Chochuwong.

There were four spots in the balance at the start of the Hong Kong Open, but all four were filled up after a dramatic first day. Ben Lane/Sean Vendy, Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard, and Chen Bo Yang/Liu Yi secured their spots.

Goh Sze Fei/Nur Izzuddin lead the qualifying list, followed by defending champions Kim Won Ho/Seo Seung Jae and Takuro Hoki/Yugo Kobayashi. World champions Liang Wei Keng/Wang Chang, who formed new partnerships after winning the world title, will be looking for their first season finale title.

Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti turned around their fortunes at the end of the qualifying period, surging from 23rd position to within the top 8 after winning the HYLO Open and making the semifinals in Hong Kong. Late qualifiers included Hsu Yin-Hui/Lin Jhih Yun and Stoeva sisters Gabriela and Stefani.

With the formerly dominant Liu Sheng Shu/Tan Ning struggling with injury, the draw appears open, with the likes of world champions Baek Ha Na/Lee So Hee, Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan, Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto and Rin Iwanaga/Kie Nakanishi performing impressively through the season.

The two most successful mixed doubles pairs on the World Tour – Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping and Jiang Zhen Bang/Wei Ya Xin – lead the qualifiers, followed by strong European contenders Mathias Christiansen/Alexandra BØje and world champions Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue.

All England champions Ye Hong Wei/Nicole Gonzales Chan and Akira Koga/Natsu Saito are among the prominent names, while Dechapol Puavaranukroh/Supissara Paewsampran and Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi secured their spots only in the final qualifying tournament.

Queensland Rugby Union and KDL Property Group Expand Partnership Through 2028
article_text:
The Queensland Rugby Union (QRU) has expanded and extended its commercial partnership with Gold Coast-based residential developer KDL Property Group through 2028, elevating the company from a junior pathways sponsor onto the elite playing kits of the Queensland Reds.

The agreement sees KDL Property Group branding appear on the playing shorts of the Queensland Reds men’s, women’s, and sevens teams for the first time. The expansion builds directly on a relationship initiated in 2024, which already includes front-of-jersey placement across Reds under-age representative squads and a three-year naming-rights commitment for the KDL Property Group Emerging Reds Cup launched in September 2026.

Commenting on the partnership, KDL Property group managing director, Kent Leicester, said: “Our involvement with Queensland rugby started with a desire to support the next generation of players and give young Queenslanders every opportunity to fulfil their potential.”

“It’s been incredibly rewarding to see that partnership develop over the past few years, and extending our support to the Queensland Reds Super Rugby and Sevens teams is a natural progression for us.

“We now support Queensland rugby right through from the junior representative pathways to the elite level, which is something I’m particularly proud of,” Leicester said.

QRU CEO, David Hanham, welcomed the commercial uplift as validation of the governing body’s long-term pathway strategy and partner engagement model.

“Kent’s genuine interest and passion to see the development of players in Queensland reach their potential is significant.”

“Having a partner that is aligned to our vision for Rugby in Queensland is important to build strong enduring relationships that ensure Rugby continues to succeed.

“We greatly appreciate the support from KDL Property Group. To now have the partnership grow to include the Reds is a great sign,” Hanham said.

In addition, the renewal integrates KDL Property Group’s brand across the entire Queensland rugby development pyramid, from regional junior carnivals at Ballymore to professional Super Rugby Pacific and international fixtures ahead of the Men’s Rugby World Cup Australia 2027.

Senior Playing Kit Inventory: Places the KDL Property Group logo on the playing shorts of the Queensland Reds men’s, women’s, and sevens squads through 2028.

Junior Representative & Cup Rights: Retains front-of-jersey sponsorship on Reds under-age teams alongside ongoing naming rights for the annual Emerging Reds Cup.

World Cup Commercial Runway: Extends brand visibility across Suncorp Stadium and international tours through the 2027 Rugby World Cup cycle.

title: Rolex keeps time for Davis Cup through extension
article_text:
World Tennis, the recently rebranded global governing body, has extended its commercial tie-up with luxury Swiss watch brand Rolex.

Through a contract extension unveiled today, Rolex will continue as a sponsor of the Davis Cup men's national teams series; the brand will keep its designation as official timekeeper of that competition.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Rolex has been in that position since 2007, while its overall involvement in tennis dates back to 1978. GlobalData Sport has valued its most recent tie-up at $1.25 million annually.

It is now, in addition to its Davis Cup involvement, it is a partner of all four Grand Slam tournaments, a sponsor of both the men's ATP and women's WTA tours, and – in addition – the official timekeeper for the Finals of the women's Billie Jean King Cup.

It also has specific agreements in place with current tennis stars Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner.

This deal has been unveiled in the build-up to the Final 8 finale of the 2026 Davis Cup, which is taking place in Bologna, Italy, between November 24 (tomorrow) and 29.

This month has already seen Yonex, the Japanese racket sports equipment brand, named as the tennis ball partner for this year's Davis Cup Final 8.

The 2026 Davis Cup Final 8 will see eight national teams compete to be crowned world champions. Alongside hosts Italy, seven winning nations from September's second-round qualifiers will participate in the event, including Czechia, Canada, South Korea, Great Britain, Germany, Austria and Spain.

International insurance company Generali Group was recently named as the new presenting partner for the Davis Cup, meanwhile.

World Tennis' commercial portfolio for the tournament also includes the likes of Visa, MG, Corpay, Fred Perry, and Betsson.

Ross Hutchins, chief executive at World Tennis, commented: "The brand is synonymous with success and prestige, and their commitment to our competition is a source of great pride for us. This news is another highlight in a year of significant commercial growth in Davis Cup as we look forward to the Final 8 this week."

World Tennis was unveiled as a rebrand of the International Tennis Federation in late June.

Arnaud Boetsch, Rolex's director of communications and image, added: "Our continued partnership with the Davis Cup by Generali reflects a relationship developed over many years, and we are proud to support the tournament and its values of team spirit, passion and sporting tradition."

The Swiss watchmaker's stable of sporting tie-ups also includes a tie-up with North American golf's top-tier PGA Tour – that deal has also been extended this month.

It also has deals in place with properties including golf's DP World Tour and World Sailing.

title: UEFA awards media rights to club competitions in 10 markets
article_text:
UEFA, European soccer’s governing body, has awarded broadcast rights to its major club competitions in 10 markets across Europe, Oceania, and the Caribbean after announcing its preferred bidders for the 2027-31 cycle.

The markets covered in this process are Australia, the Caribbean, Cyprus, the Dominican Republic, Greece, Iceland, Israel, Malta, New Zealand, and Türkiye.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Rights have been awarded for the elite UEFA Champions League (UCL), secondary Europa League, and third-tier Conference League for the next four seasons, from 2027-28 through 2030-31.

The process, described as “highly competitive”, included incumbent broadcasters, new market entrants, global digital platforms as well as local pay and free-to-air channels. New partners were secured in five of the 10 markets.

In Australia, all UCL rights have been snapped up by international sports streaming giant DAZN, which includes Foxtel and Kayo Sports.

DAZN has also landed rights to all three club competitions in Israel.

Elsewhere in Europe, rights to all club competitions have been secured by free-to-air (FTA) broadcaster Skai in Greece, pay-TV operator Cyta in Cyprus (with public-service broadcaster CYBC to show UCL Tuesday first pick games on a co-exclusive basis), digital streaming platform Exxen in Turkey, and cable pay-TV broadcaster Melita in Malta, with the semi-finals and finals of each competition to be shown FTA by the government-owned public broadcaster PBS.

CYBC will now provide free coverage of the UCL in Cyprus after previously having rights to the Europa League and Conference League, while Exxen returns as the rightsholder in Turkey, taking over from public-service broadcaster TRT.

In Iceland, streaming service Viaplay will keep UCL rights, while OTT platform Livey has acquired the Europa League and Conference League.

In the Caribbean, CPSL has retained rights to the UCL, Europa League, and Conference League, with ATV having all rights in Suriname co-exclusively. CPSL’s deal also covers the Dominican Republic.

Broadcast partners for the Europa League and Conference League in Australia, and for all three competitions in New Zealand, have been awarded to a preferred bidder but will be announced at a later date.

As well as Viaplay and CPSL, the deals with CYTA, Melita and PBS are also renewals.

UEFA went to market in all 10 territories at the end of September, with a deadline for submissions of November 3.

The tender process was managed by the UC3 commercial arm, a joint venture between UEFA and the European Football Clubs' body, and Relevant Football partners, UEFA’s sales agency for the club competitions through 2033, spanning media, sponsorship, and licensing rights.

Sportcal (GlobalData Sport) understands Relevent’s third and final multi-market tender concluded with an average uplift of around 150% across the 10 markets, which represents the strongest result of the 2027-31 media rights cycle so far for the agency.

Just 12 months after Relevent opened the process with its tender for Europe's top five markets in late 2025, only a small number of markets remain to be finalised.

These are Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Gibraltar, the Indian Subcontinent, Montenegro, North Macedonia, the Pacific Islands, Serbia, Slovenia and Ukraine.

title: WSL and member clubs agree on central betting sponsor ban
article_text:
English women's soccer's top-tier WSL has an agreement in place with its clubs that it will not take on betting brands as commercial partners at league level.

An announcement was made regarding this decision late last week by the WSL Football body, which governs both the 14-team WSL and the 12-team WSL 2.

For the WSL, Barclays Bank has title-sponsored the league since 2019-20, with other main partners including Airbnb, British Gas, Tesco, EA FC, and Mercedes-Benz.

The Tesco deal was the last of these agreements to be unveiled, with a multi-year deal between the two parties announced in late September.

The 2026-27 WSL campaign got underway on September 4 and will run through May 23.

WSL Football, owned by its member clubs, was set up in August 2024 and controls the top two leagues. During its first year as a standalone organization – ending in July 2025 – it recorded an operating loss of £8.2 million (at the time, $11.3 million).

title: Why MLB could be the first major league to move its championship to streaming
article_text:
It’s not a question of if, but when the first major American professional sports league puts its championship exclusively on a streaming service. Based on timing and the value of that championship, Major League Baseball is in the perfect position to make that decision, but only if it chooses.

Streaming services have quickly become major players in the American sports media rights space. Prime Video now has rights to the NFL, NBA, and NASCAR. Peacock is saturated with MLB, NBA, Premier League, and basketball and football from the Big Ten. Netflix has rights to MLB and NFL, and will exclusively air the 2027 Women’s FIFA World Cup in the United States and Canada (and could soon secure rights to the 2030 men’s World Cup).

But none of those rights include championship games, except Netflix and the Women’s World Cup. The NFL, MLB, and NBA have gone as far as to put playoff games on streamers (the entirety of the 2027 NBA Eastern Conference Final will air on Prime Video), but the Big Four leagues have not gone all the way yet.

There is good reason to believe, however, that could soon change. Both the NHL and MLB will see their media rights expire after the 2028 season (if there is a lockout, the MLB contracts could go through 2029). Streamers have already shown interest in both leagues. NHL games air on ESPN Unlimited and Hulu, while MLB games stream across Netflix, Peacock, and Apple TV.

With the NFL and NBA locked into relatively longer contracts, based on timing alone, the league to make the streaming jump first for its championship could be the NHL or MLB.

The NHL’s public comments have already tipped their hand; not necessarily that they are about to deal the Stanley Cup Final to a streamer, but that they are looking for a significant media rights increase, 50% to 100% more, according to CNBC. The NHL currently makes around $650 million annually from its U.S. media contracts.

While MLB has not indicated so publicly, the league will likely look for an increase in a similar range. That has been the norm in media rights recently. The NBA’s latest contracts saw an increase more in the range of 150%.

One of the reasons the NBA was able to get such an increase is that the league was willing to put key inventory on streaming. Games on Peacock and Prime are key components of the NBA’s agreement. As previously mentioned, both services air playoff games, and Prime goes as far as the conference finals.

The other key reason the NBA got its increase was competition. ESPN, Prime, NBC, and TNT were four media companies competing for three packages. Having more bidders than packages drove up the price for the NBA. If either league truly wants to maximize its next national deal, it needs to incentivize competition for its key media rights packages. Allowing streamers to bid on their championship inventory could be that incentive.

MLB has already carved out a streaming package of key rights for Netflix, featuring Opening Night, the Home Run Derby, and a special-event game. The league has shown a willingness to put important inventory on streaming already, which could signal a willingness to shop the World Series.

But why MLB instead of the NHL? MLB has more to gain because the World Series is more popular than the Stanley Cup Final. This year’s World Series averaged 11.83 million viewers on Fox; the Stanley Cup Final averaged less than half that, 5.27 million viewers on ABC (which was the most-watched since 2019).

MLB has also historically been far more reliant on revenue from the collapsing local TV business than the NHL, NFL, and NBA. A 2023 Sportico report found that local media, including radio, accounts for 23% of MLB team revenue. With revenue from the regional sports network business drying up, MLB will have more incentive to maximize its national media rights revenue.

There are some clear risks for MLB if it goes down this path, however. By going to streaming, MLB would make its games less accessible and likely hurt its viewership, at least in the near term. The reach of broadcast television is still unmatched for live sports viewership, though streamers have closed the gap in recent years for major events like Netflix’s Christmas Day games or Prime Video’s Thursday Night Football.

There’s also the PR nightmare moving the World Series to streaming would create. Whichever league moves its championship to a streamer first is going to have to put up with some very angry fans and some terrible press coverage. Polling shows that Americans are extremely unhappy with sports fragmentation, and that was with no league championships on streaming.

Not to mention, the federal government has taken interest in slowing the shift of live sports from broadcast to streaming. MLB, like other pro sports leagues, enjoys a federal antitrust exemption that could be put in jeopardy should the league make an aggressive move towards streaming.

So, there is no guarantee that either the NHL or MLB will move their championships to a streamer, even on a partial basis. The NHL may be wary because of its decision to split the Stanley Cup Final between over-the-air television (ABC) and cable (TNT) has not paid off from a viewership standpoint.

But with national media rights becoming even more important, and the World Series still holding incredible value, the league will at least consider selling it to a streamer, if only to test the market.

Meta inks 49ers sponsorship, will give away AI glasses

title: Esso partners NHL in Germany for Dusseldorf international games
article_text:
North America’s elite National Hockey League (NHL) has announced a new partnership with Esso, the prominent retail petrol and diesel brand, covering the German market.

Esso becomes an official partner of the NHL in Germany, gaining marketing rights including virtual slot in-ice advertising and digitally enhanced dashboard placement on NHL regular-season broadcasts in Germany.

Marketing rights will extend to the upcoming pair of two regular-season NHL games set to take place in Germany next month, the NHL Global Series Germany, which will see the Ottawa Senators play two games in Dusseldorf against the Chicago Blackhawks, on December 18 and 20.

“Esso’s marketing support will help us reach fans in new and creative ways in Germany, and we look forward to delivering exceptional fan experiences through our relationship."

Esso's parent company Imperial Oil has been associated with the NHL since 1936, and in 2018, it became the official retail fuel of the NHL in the Canadian market. Now, by expanding its coverage to a priority international territory, it has entrenched itself in the league’s sponsorship platform.

Around one-third of the total number of contracted NHL players are European, of whom seven are German, including Edmonton Oilers forward and five-time all-star Leon Draisaitl, making the DACH region specifically one of the league's targeted growth areas.

The international games in Dusseldorf this season will be presented by Kaufland, through a deal announced earlier this month. title: ITV lands Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 rights
article_text:
ITV will be the exclusive UK broadcaster of the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, with Birmingham’s own Alison Hammond and Paralympian Ade Adepitan co-hosting the opening and closing ceremonies.

The Games run from 10th to 17th July 2027 and will bring together 550 competitors from 26 nations across 12 adaptive sports, alongside 1,100 family members and supporters. A further 30,000 spectators are expected each day.

ITV’s free-to-air coverage will include both ceremonies, daily highlights programmes and exclusive digital content across ITVX, ITV YouTube and ITV’s social channels. Livewire Pictures will produce the host broadcast, covering all 12 sports and the ceremonies for audiences worldwide.

The deal was confirmed on ITV’s This Morning, where Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, appeared alongside former competitors Josh Boggi and Jules Bale. The appearance also marked key milestones in the build-up, including the launch of general sale tickets, volunteer recruitment and the growth of the INSPIRE education programme, which has now engaged nearly 50,000 young learners.

Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, Patron of the Invictus Games Foundation, said, “Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham was the place where so many of our competitors, who were critically wounded in Iraq and Afghanistan, woke up. So the first people they would see were the nurses and doctors in Queen Elizabeth Hospital. For them to come back with me and go back there was a really brilliant moving moment. Hundreds of British soldiers were treated at Queen Elizabeth Hospital. So for them to be going back to the Games in that city means a lot. I don’t think there’s a city in the UK that means so much to them. It’s the right place for it.”

Birmingham was chosen to host because of its long connection to the recovery and rehabilitation of the Armed Forces community. The city is home to Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham and the Royal Centre for Defence Medicine.

Katie Rawcliffe, Director of Entertainment, Reality & Daytime Commissioning at ITV, said, “The Invictus Games is such a beloved event and, we couldn’t be prouder at ITV to be the exclusive UK broadcaster. Our extensive coverage will extend across ITV, ITVX and ITV YouTube for our viewers to enjoy free-to-air, ensuring they do not miss a minute of the action.”

Vicky Gosling, Chair of Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, said, “Having ITV as our exclusive broadcast partner is a major milestone for Birmingham 2027. ITV’s commitment reflects the strength of the Invictus Games, the importance of the stories we have to tell and the appetite among UK audiences to hear them. Together, we can bring the recovery journeys of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans to millions of people, building understanding and support for the community at the heart of our Games.”

This news come after Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 confirmed the continuation of its partnership with Ottobock, which will provide technical support for competitors during the Games in the UK.

title: REDMAGIC Expands Global Esports Presence with Sponsorship of 2026 PUBG MOBILE Global Championship
article_text:
Building on its longstanding involvement in esports, REDMAGIC brings its tournament sponsorship to the global stage, showcasing its flagship gaming performance at one of mobile esports’ premier events.

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — REDMAGIC, a gaming technology brand renowned for its performance-driven innovations, has joined the 2026 PUBG MOBILE Global Championship (2026 PMGC) as its Official Gaming Phone Sponsor. The partnership marks a new milestone in REDMAGIC’s esports journey, bringing its advanced gaming technology to one of the world’s premier competitive gaming stages and reaffirming its commitment to the global gaming community.

Organised by KRAFTON and Level Infinite, 2026 PMGC marks the culmination of the PUBG MOBILE competitive season, bringing together 39 teams from around the world. The championship will take place in Istanbul, Türkiye, with the Grand Finals scheduled for December 11–13, 2026, at the Turkcell Basketbol Gelişim Merkezi. The 16 qualifying teams will compete over three days, with six matches scheduled each day, for the world championship title and a share of the US$3 million prize pool. The tournament will culminate in the crowning of the world champion on the final day.

Forrest Pan, Head of Global Business, highlighted the importance of delivering smooth, responsive, and stable gameplay experiences for PUBG MOBILE players. He emphasised how precision, speed, and reliable performance enable players to stay focused, react swiftly, and perform at their best in high-pressure competitive environments.

“At REDMAGIC, we believe great technology gives players the confidence to put their skills to the test,” he said. “Our liquid cooling technology helps unlock the full potential of the Snapdragon processor, while long-lasting battery life keeps players in the game. A high-refresh-rate display and responsive touch controls deliver the clarity and precision that competitive gaming demands.”

“Our collaboration with PUBG MOBILE reflects REDMAGIC’s commitment to pushing the boundaries of mobile gaming through purposeful innovation,” he added. “Guided by our mission to help gamers win more games, we continue to develop powerful and reliable hardware that supports players when it matters most.”

Through its collaboration with PUBG MOBILE, REDMAGIC brings its gaming technology to the professional esports stage, connecting competitive players and fans through their shared passion for performance.

At the heart of REDMAGIC’s sponsorship is the REDMAGIC 11S Pro, an award-winning gaming smartphone recognised by international technology media for its performance and gaming capabilities. Designed with professional esports athletes in mind, the device combines high-performance processing, advanced thermal management, and dedicated gaming controls to meet the demands of competitive mobile gaming.

Powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Leading Version and REDMAGIC’s dedicated RedCore R4 gaming chip, the device delivers powerful processing and smooth, responsive gameplay. Its AquaCore Cooling System integrates liquid cooling, a 13,116mm² 3D vapor chamber, Composite Liquid Metal 3.0, and a 24,000 RPM turbo fan to help maintain performance during intensive gaming sessions.

The 6.85-inch BOE X10 AMOLED display features a refresh rate of up to 144Hz, instant touch sampling of up to 3,000Hz, and dedicated 520Hz shoulder triggers for precise, responsive controls. A 7,500mAh battery with 80W wired and wireless fast charging further supports extended gaming sessions, making the REDMAGIC 11S Pro a powerful companion for competitive mobile gaming.

REDMAGIC’s partnership with 2026 PMGC builds on its previous involvement in China’s esports scene, extending its support for competitive gaming to the international stage. As the Official Gaming Phone Sponsor, REDMAGIC will showcase the REDMAGIC 11S Pro at the 2026 PMGC event, further strengthening its connection with the global PUBG MOBILE community.

The partnership will take centre stage at the 2026 PMGC Grand Finals in Istanbul, where 16 qualifying teams will compete over three days for the world championship title and a share of the US$3 million prize pool. As the culminating event of the 2026 PUBG MOBILE esports season, the Grand Finals will bring together top teams from around the world for the season’s ultimate showdown.

REDMAGIC continues to push the boundaries of mobile gaming, delivering innovations in performance, cooling, and gaming technology with each new generation. The newly launched REDMAGIC 12 Pro reflects this commitment, combining next-generation hardware with advanced cooling solutions and gamer-focused features designed to deliver an elevated gaming experience. Now officially available, the REDMAGIC 12 Pro marks another milestone in the brand’s pursuit of high-performance mobile gaming.

To learn more about REDMAGIC and the REDMAGIC 12 Pro, visit redmagic.gg

We established REDMAGIC in 2018 with the dream of making it the world’s brand of choice for mobile gaming. Our motto, Win More Games, is brought to life by our collection of gaming gear that includes gaming phones and accessories, as well as PC equipment and devices to keep you connected to the internet. REDMAGIC has built a solid reputation with gamers worldwide for its performance, and we’ve amassed a global reach of 50 countries and regions to make us one of the best gaming smartphone manufacturers in the market.

PUBG MOBILE is based on PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS, the phenomenon that took the world of interactive entertainment by storm in 2017. Up to 100 players parachute onto a remote island to battle in a winner-takes-all showdown. Players must locate and scavenge their own weapons, vehicles, and supplies, and defeat every player in a visually and tactically rich battleground that forces players into a shrinking play zone. PUBG MOBILE is co-developed by LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS of Tencent Games and KRAFTON, Inc.
