title: Court ruling hands African football trophy back to Senegal
Argentina name two SVNS debutants in star-studded squad
article_text:
Two potential HSBC SVNS Series debutants have been included in Argentina’s squad for Dubai and Cape Town, with Santiago Alvarez and Luciano Gonzalez the most experienced members of a squad that has played 389 events between them.

La Plata-product Luca Julian is set to wear a Los Pumas Sevens jersey for the first time, while Francisco Calello is also set for a maiden appearance on the SVNS Series. Calello did get to play for the national sevens team at the recent South American Championship in Cordoba.

Alvarez is the most-experienced player in the Los Pumas Sevens squad, with the forward set to earn his 79th tournament cap. Gonzalez has featured in 72 SVNS events, while Santiago Mare and Marcos Moneta have played at least 42 tournaments each.

Moneta was the top try-scorer on the SVNS Series last season, while Gonzalez earned Dream Team honours after another exceptional season. Argentina didn’t win any titles last season but did claim silver twice, and bronze another two times.

Argentina have been drawn in Pool A along with two-time reigning SVNS World Championship winners South Africa, Australia, and the United States. Los Pumas Sevens get their new campaign underway against the Blitzboks at 4:52 am on Saturday morning (Argentine time).

title: Olympic hero set for SVNS milestone as Blitzboks name Dubai squad
article_text:
Paris Olympics bronze medallist Selvyn Davids will reach an HSBC SVNS Series milestone when the new season begins this weekend, with the playmaker in line to earn his 50th tournament cap as South Africa return to Dubai.

Davids famously set up the match-winner as South Africa defeated Australia in the battle for bronze at the Paris Games. The 32-year-old broke down the left sideline before handing the ball off to Shaun Williams within the in-goal.

Coach Philip Snyman has included two potential debutants in a 13-man squad for the SVNS Series season opener in Dubai. JC Mars and Van Reenan Kruger are both in line to play on the world’s premier sevens circuit for the very first time.

Siviwe Soyizwapi will lead the Blitzboks in the absence of regular skipper Impi Visser, who was not available for selection. Soyizwapi will be supported by 65-event veteran Ryan Oothuizen, 60-event forward Zain Davids, and former captain Davids.

“He is just such an awesome team player and playmaker and to have him fit and ready is just great,” Snyman said.

“The same with Siviwe, who will take the reins with Impi not quite fit and available for this tournament. One of our strengths is a strong leadership group, which makes my life much easier as a coach.”

Christie Grobbelaar, Ricardo Duarttee, Quewin Nortje, Dewald Human, Grant de Jager and Sebastiaan Job have been included in the lineup, along with reigning World Rugby Sevens Player of the Year Tristan Leyds.

South Africa won five Dubai titles in a row before that streak came to an end two years ago, with Fiji emerging victorious. New Zealand are currently the defending champions, with the South Africans recording a sixth-place finish last season.

But the Blitzboks went on to dominate the regular season, securing the SVNS Series league title with some inspirational performances in Cape Town, Perth, Vancouver and New York. They then went on to claim the World Championship crown during a dramatic SVNS Bordeaux.

“Last season we blooded six new players and they all delivered, and after all of our pre-season camps, I saw enough in ‘Van’ and JC to confidently select them for this trip,” the coach added.

“JC has been in the SA Rugby pathway since his school days, while ‘Van’ had a brilliant Varsity Cup campaign and once we brought them into the wider group, they quickly rose to the challenge.”

title: USGA, R&A provide significant update to golf equipment changes: Answering 5 burning questions
article_text:
The latest twist in the golf ball rollback saga has arrived.

Late last week, the USGA and R&A quietly released a “notice to manufacturers” indicating they have identified two paths to limit distance gains in professional golf and are targeting approval of those changes in time for the start of the new PGA Tour schedule in 2028.

At first glance, the changes outlined by the governing bodies aim to limit distance gains for pro players with the driver and golf ball, but appear to fall short of the distance drops targeted by the golf ball rollback standard initially pursued back in 2023.

But let’s hold on for a second. If you’re a golfer with a normal degree of exposure to governing body minutiae, you’ve probably got no idea what I just said. So let’s get you the goods without the headache in Q&A form.

The USGA and R&A have been looking to curb distance in pro golf for years … but as it turns out, it’s pretty hard to curb distance! Players hate it. Club companies hate it. Regular golfers hate it. The governing bodies don’t even seem to like it.

In fact, it might be said that curbing distance in golf is a lot like eating chard — if it’s so good for you, why does it taste like that?!

The USGA and R&A are unusual in that they are self-aware enough to recognize their chard-iness. They have tried very hard to find a solution to the distance problem that will satisfy everyone or, at least, annoy everyone the least.

First the USGA and R&A pitched a golf ball rollback that would only affect Tour pros. That led to a mutiny. Then, in late 2023, they pitched a rollback for all golfers, pro and recreational. Another mutiny. THEN, in early 2026, they announced a sudden agreement with the PGA Tour to work toward new solutions to curb distance while pushing back the deadline for the rollback-for-all to 2030. No mutiny this time … well, except for all the regular golfers who understood a rollback was necessary to preserve the sport in its purest form. Among that crew? Yep, you guessed it: Mutiny.

Now we have last week’s announcement, which appears to show plans to cut back driver AND golf ball distance … but by what sounds like a smaller margin than the original all-golfer rollback. That’s good news if you didn’t want to lose 15 yards every time you teed off at Bethpage with your buddies. It’s good news if you’re a pro golfer who didn’t want to lose 15 yards at the Masters. And it’s good news if you’re the USGA and R&A and you know you’ve gotta do something to stop the steady creep of distance increases.

2. What is the change the USGA and R&A are promoting?

Basically, they want to make their equipment tests harder to pass. Right now, the equipment companies have wiggle room in how their golf balls and drivers get tested. When the ball is tested, it has a three-yard buffer where it can travel beyond the legal threshold without “failing” the test. When the driver face is tested, it has an 18-microsecond buffer where it can spring beyond the legal threshold without “failing” the test.

Under the changes proposed by the USGA and R&A, which would go into effect in 2028, the driver face and golf ball would be required to stay at or below the legal limit. Considering those changes aren’t aspiring to lessen the distance standard — just test it more stringently — it seems unlikely the changes will produce a considerable distance loss with the golf ball or driver. But a better fence would theoretically defend against continued increases in ball flight.

3. Would *my* golf ball travel shorter if this rule passed?

Nope! These changes are “model local rules,” which means they would be enforced only for the pro tours that choose to adopt them, and not for everyday Joes like you and me.

4. What about that other golf ball rollback? The one you guys have spent three years telling me about?

The rollback for all golfers is still scheduled to go into effect in 2030. That plan, which would change the testing thresholds to lower driving distance for everybody, in theory losing as much as 15 yards off the drives of the longest-hitters, is still ongoing. But it might be on the brink of changing. The 2030 test conditions are being revised, and last week’s notice committed to giving “updated test conditions” to club manufacturers. Earlier this year, GOLF reported that the change could involve the shape of drivers and/or the thickness of the driver face.

At a time of considerable change in professional golf, new distance standards represent the most seismic shift to the game as golfers know it. For years, elite-level players have been gaining distance off the tee — changes driven at least in part by advancements in golf ball and driver technology. These changes, which have changed the way pro golf is played at the highest levels, have concerned the governing bodies responsible for upholding golf’s traditions, its courses and itssense of competitive fairness.

Beyond the historical record and scoring implications of players hitting the ball farther than ever, these changes have threatened many of golf’s most historic tournament hosts. Changes to driving distance have forced many of the world’s best golf courses to undergo costly expansions in order to host high-level men’s events, and have all but eliminated many other historic courses from consideration for such events.

title: LIV Golf profane domain names freed up following tour’s demise
article_text:
A tranche of domain names, including livgolfmyass.com, livgolfsucks.com and terroristgolfleague.com, bought up by LIV Golf to prevent critics creating insulting websites could now become available following the company’s liquidation.

The revelation shows how sensitive LIV Golf chiefs were when the controversial league, backed by billions from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, launched in 2022. LIV Golf collapsed after PIF withdrew funding in April.

This column recently revealed that executives were paid millions of pounds before the league filed for bankruptcy, while unsecured creditors, including a UK charity that uses sport to change the lives of vulnerable young people, are not expected to receive a penny back. The Change Foundation, based in Surrey, is owed £22,200.

Executives had hoped a rescue package led by BC Partners would save the league, but the private equity firm walked away due to concerns over the lack of elite players prepared to participate in “LIV 2.0”.

It may be music to the ears of detractors who may – or, indeed, may not – have tried to set up critical websites, only to discover LIV Golf had beaten them to it. Also among the 874 domain names LIV officials bought to keep them out of the hands of naysayers were bloodmoneygolf.com, corruptgolf.com and livgolfracist.com.

LIV Golf did not respond to a request for comment.

The London Stadium has been given the green light to host mega-fights after Newham Council indicated it would grant planning permission to increase its capacity for boxing events.

This column revealed in October that London Stadium bosses wanted restrictions relaxed to allow it to rival Wembley for blockbuster fights and help offset losses from anchor tenant West Ham’s relegation to the Championship.

As part of a wider planning application, officials requested that boxing be classified as a unique one-off event rather than a sport, which limits capacity to 60,000. Newham Council has now resolved to grant permission, subject to final sign-off on the planning agreement.

The stadium has become a £19m-per-year burden on taxpayers since West Ham were relegated from the Premier League in the summer but boxing could help soften the blow.

Anthony Joshua’s upcoming fight against Tyson Fury at the 80,000-seater Principality Stadium is expected to generate more than £20m. Under new terms, a fight night at the London Stadium could accommodate up to 85,000 fans if it is selected in one of eight slots for maximum capacity, while regular events would still be able to sell 80,000 tickets.

The council has requested that London Stadium officials make reasonable efforts to give 100 tickets to local residents.

Newcastle United are still spending money on determining whether to expand St James’ Park or build a new home three years into the project and despite being forced to sell many of their best players in the summer, City AM can reveal.

Sources with knowledge of the situation say both stadium options remain under active consideration. Building a new 65,000-seater ground from scratch at Leazes Park, a Grade II-listed site adjacent to St James’ Park and owned by Newcastle City Council, would be expected to cost around £1.5bn.

Expanding the existing stadium from 52,700 to 60,000 would be a considerably cheaper option at around £500m. The club continues to consult external advisers as it assesses the best course of action.

Newcastle were forced to sell key players in the summer, generating around £240m through the sales of Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, Sandro Tonali to Spurs and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

When Brighton and Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom makes a prediction, he rarely gets it wrong. Now the man who built a fortune by beating the odds through his data-driven betting operation, Starlizard, has predicted that Brighton will qualify for the Champions League.

It would be easy to get carried away with Brighton’s flying start to this season. They have emerged as surprise early challengers at the top of the table, outscoring everyone and beating Arsenal and Manchester City, two of the dominant forces of recent years.

But Bloom is a cool calculator, so a prediction made during an Overcoming Multiple Sclerosis event at the Amex Stadium recently should not be taken lightly.

Aston Villa are considering scrapping their in-house TV channel’s £30 annual subscription fee for season-ticket holders and members after it was pointed out by fans that rival clubs offer a similar service for free.

Currently, season-ticket holders, who pay upwards of £700 per season, receive access to Aston Villa TV at half price. But Villa, who are set to earn at least £50m from playing in this season’s Champions League, will discuss removing the 58p-per-week charge for season-ticket holders and members next year.

title: Brooks Koepka Aims Yet Another Dig At Bryson DeChambeau
article_text:
Brooks Koepka just can't help himself when it comes to aiming jibes at Bryson DeChambeau, with his latest coming in the build-up to The Skins Game this Friday.

The Farmers Insurance Skins Game will be shown on Prime Video on Friday 27 November with Koepka taking on Justin Thomas, Wyndham Clark and Jackson Koivun at Atlantic Fields Golf Club in Florida.

But although there will be plenty of trash talking between the foursome as they battle it out for $4m - the biggest dig landed in the pre-event press conference was aimed at someone not even taking part.

Koepka was asked about a similar event - The Showdown in 2024 - when he teamed up with DeChambeau in a sign their long-running fued had been squashed.

However, reflecting on that heavy defeat to Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler in the $10m crypto contest Koepka again showed there's no love lost between the two.

"Since I did not win, my teammate didn't hole a putt the entire time, so I did not receive any of that," said Koepka.

"Which is great because it's an individual thing this time. So I'm more excited about that, but it'll be fun."

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

Koepka was also keen to point out he "didn't get to choose" his teammate for that last head-to-head contest.

From fierce enemies to teammates in both the Ryder Cup and then The Showdown, Koepka and DeChambeau were never best buddies but their relationship seemed cordial until recently.

Asked about DeChambeau's experience alongside McIlroy during the final round of the 2025 Masters, Koepka was equally as scathing.

DeChambeau complained about McIlroy blanking him at Augusta National as he finally ended his search for a Green Jacket - with the Northern Irishman wondering why he'd be so chatty when history was on the line.

It was clear which side Koepka was on when he said "I don't think many people want to talk to him regardless" in reference to DeChambeau.

Koepka also said DeChambeau "lives in his own world" during that interview with Skratch's Dan Rapaport and it's clear the two personalties simply don't mix.

DeChambeau is seen more on YouTube than the golf course these days, but if the two ever tee it up in the same event again it'll be one to watch.

Paul Higham is a sports journalist with over 20 years of experience in covering most major sporting events for both Sky Sports and BBC Sport. He is currently freelance and covers the golf majors on the BBC Sport website. Highlights over the years include covering that epic Monday finish in the Ryder Cup at Celtic Manor and watching Rory McIlroy produce one of the most dominant Major wins at the 2011 US Open at Congressional. He also writes betting previews and still feels strangely proud of backing Danny Willett when he won the Masters in 2016 - Willett also praised his putting stroke during a media event before the Open at Hoylake. Favourite interviews he's conducted have been with McIlroy, Paul McGinley, Thomas Bjorn, Rickie Fowler and the enigma that is Victor Dubuisson. A big fan of watching any golf from any tour, sadly he spends more time writing about golf than playing these days with two young children, and as a big fair weather golfer claims playing in shorts is worth at least five shots. Being from Liverpool he loves the likes of Hoylake, Birkdale and the stretch of tracks along England's Golf Coast, but would say his favourite courses played are Kingsbarns and Portrush.

title: Smashing Stats: Syed Modi International 2026
article_text:
Syed Modi India International 2026 is the final HSBC BWF World Tour event of the year before attention turns to the season-ending finale in Hangzhou.

Let’s look at some intriguing facts and figures about the Super 300 event.

- Treesa Jolly/Gayatri Gopichand Pullela and Tanisha Crasto are the only top seeded players to taste previous glory.

- Crasto, however, claimed her title in 2022 with Ishaan Bhatnagar and will partner Dhruv Kapila this time.

- Jolly/Pullela are the only defending champions in the field.

- Retaining their title would make them the most successful women’s pair in tournament history.

- They will also become the first players in any category to win three seasons in a row.

- India are the sole nation with seeds in every department this year.

- Among them are men’s pair Hariharan Amsakarunan/M.R. Arjun, who will look to end India’s wait for a crown in the discipline since the tournament began in 2009.

- Top seeds Raymond Indra/Nikolaus Joaquin, meanwhile, could help Indonesia move ahead of China as the most successful nation in men’s doubles, with a fourth victory.

- The only other former winner in the draw is Malaysian Muhammad Haikal, who partners Junaidi Arif after winning men’s doubles in 2023 with Choong Hon Jian.

- Malaysia, yet to win men’s singles, have two seeds this year – Lee Zii Jia (2) and Justin Hoh (5).

Standout Stat: Should Riko Gunji ace women’s singles like her compatriot Hina Akechi last year, Japan will become the second nation other than India to keep the crown in the category.

title: Australian Sports Commission and Getty Images Launch Inclusive Community Sport Visual Library
article_text:
The Australian Sports Commission (ASC) has partnered with global visual content creator Getty Images to launch a dedicated visual library designed to modernise how grassroots sport is represented across Australia.

The collection is delivered under Play Well, Australia’s first national sport participation strategy, co-designed with the sector in 2023, and debuts with 250 authentic still images and videos spanning athletics, equestrian, netball, badminton, and football. By resolving a long-standing marketing bottleneck for national sporting organisations (NSOs) and local clubs, the initiative supplies sector-wide communications teams with representative promotional assets ahead of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

ASC executive general manager of sport system impact and chair of the Play Well Leadership Group, Richard McInnes, highlighted the commercial and participation impact of equipping sports with authentic visual storytelling tools.

“Play Well is built on the belief that everyone has a place in sport.”

“We know the way sport is represented can influence whether people feel welcome and believe there is a place for them.

“This partnership will give sporting organisations access to authentic images, to use in promotional material and communication, that actually reflects the diversity of the people, communities and experiences that make Australian sport so special.

“It is another practical step towards breaking down barriers to participation and ensuring more people can see themselves being involved in sport,” McInnes said.

Getty Images senior director of custom and creative partnerships, Svetlana Zhukova, emphasised the role of representative media in reshaping community perceptions ahead of Brisbane 2032.

“Sport has an extraordinary ability to connect people, but the images used to represent it don’t always reflect who is actually taking part.”

“Through the partnership, we’re giving sports organisations, media and communities access to imagery that better reflects the diversity of Australian sport as the country looks towards Brisbane 2032,” Zhukova said.

Produced in collaboration with community clubs and inclusion bodies—including Sport Inclusion Australia, Metropolitan Districts Netball Association, Footscray Rangers Football Club, and Melbourne Smashers Badminton, the library reflects diverse ages, cultural backgrounds, genders, and physical abilities. Sporting bodies and sector partners can request direct access to the asset bank via the ASC marketing team, with additional sports scheduled for production and integration throughout 2027.

title: World Rugby Appoints Heinz as Official Condiment Supplier for Rugby World Cups 2027 and 2029
article_text:
World Rugby has appointed food manufacturer Heinz as Official Condiment Supplier across both the Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 and Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029 in Australia.

The multi-tournament agreement integrates Heinz’s core table sauce portfolio, including Heinz Ketchup and Mayonnaise, into stadium foodservice operations and official Fan Festivals across all seven Australian host cities.

The partnership expands World Rugby’s fast-moving consumer goods roster for its consecutive Australian tournament cycle, joining Principal Partners Asahi, Emirates, and Visa alongside fellow Official Suppliers and Supporters including Gilbert, Macron, Ticketmaster, Unilever, and Woolworths.

Men’s Rugby World Cup managing director, Chris Stanley, highlighted the value of partnering with a household food manufacturer ahead of the largest men’s tournament to date.

“We are thrilled to welcome Heinz, a historic and treasured brand, as an Official Supplier for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 and Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029.”

“As rugby continues to grow its international footprint, it’s an exciting opportunity to partner with a renowned food manufacturer and supplier like Heinz, who will help us deliver both tournaments and create more pathways to grow the sport in Australia and worldwide.

“Heinz has a longstanding legacy of serving up much loved sauces and condiments to families and households across the globe, so we are delighted to have the company on board as we get set to deliver two iconic Rugby World Cups.

“With less than one year to go until next year’s tournament, it’s an exciting time to join the partner family as we prepare to host the biggest edition of Men’s Rugby World Cup to date,” Stanley said.

Heinz ANZ chief marketing officer, Michael Magee, emphasised the natural alignment between match-day hospitality and the brand’s multi-generational Australian heritage.

“Sport has an incredible ability to bring people together, and food has always been part of how fans experience those big game day moments.”

“As a brand that has been part of Australian mealtimes for generations, we’re incredibly proud to partner with Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 and Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029 – particularly on home soil. From the pre-match build-up to the final whistle, we’ll be there to bring the flavour and make every win taste even better,” Magee said.

Landing with less than 12 months remaining before the expanded 24-team Men’s Rugby World Cup kicks off across six weeks from 1 October to 13 November 2027, the agreement capitalises on strong early commercial demand, with more than 1.3 million tickets already sold.

Dual-Tournament Official Supplier Rights: Grants Heinz category exclusivity as Official Condiment Supplier for both Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 and Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029.

Seven-City Venue & Fan Festival Supply: Deploys Heinz Ketchup, Mayonnaise, and table sauces across all match venues and official Fan Festivals throughout Australia’s seven host cities.

Commercial Runway & Ticket Momentum: Anchors brand activation ahead of the 1 October – 13 November 2027 men’s tournament, which has already surpassed 1.3 million tickets sold across its 24-team format.

title: Weightlifting and Wrestling Sign Sponsorship Deals Worth Up to 1.4 Billion Won Over Three Years with IBK
article_text:
The Korean Weightlifting Federation and the Korea Wrestling Federation have signed official sponsorship agreements with IBK Industrial Bank of Korea.

Yesterday, on November 24, the two federations signed agreements at the IBK headquarters in Euljiro, Seoul, securing up to 1.4 billion won in financial support over the next three years.

This agreement continues the sponsorship that began with their initial partnership in 2022. The funds will be used for domestic and overseas training camps for national team athletes ahead of major international events including the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, as well as for improving training environments, fostering promising young athletes, and promoting grassroots sports.

Choi Sung-yong, president of the Korean Weightlifting Federation, expressed gratitude for the bank's continued support, stating that they will do their utmost to help athletes make a greater leap forward and achieve valuable results ahead of the LA Olympics.

Chang Min-young, president of IBK, stated that the bank will lend its support so that athletes can fully showcase their skills and future prospects can nurture their dreams.

title: Rights to next WBC will be negotiated alongside broader MLB package
article_text:
Coming off of a record-setting performance in the United States, negotiations for rights to the next World Baseball Classic will coincide with Major League Baseball’s broader media rights talks.

Rights to broadcast the next World Baseball Classic will be negotiated alongside the broader Major League Baseball rights packages in 2028, Sports Media Watch has learned. WBC rights have historically been sold separately, but MLB will have the opportunity to add the WBC to conversations that are already expected to include its full suite of local, national and global rights.

MLB commissioner Rob Manfred signaled as much on “The Dan Patrick Show” earlier this month: “Our broadcast partners were out in force at the WBC finals and I think this is going to be a piece of our national broadcasting agreements.”

Manfred conditioned that statement on the event shifting to a regular rotation: “Obviously to do that it has to be on a regular schedule.” The WBC has taken place every three or four years since its inception in 2006, and it is not immediately clear whether the next edition will be in 2029 or 2030.

Rights to this past year’s WBC were officially set mere months in advance, with Fox Sports’ deal to acquire U.S. rights announced last October. It is unclear whether the company had any competition for the event, which ended up delivering audiences in the neighborhood of World Series games.

Netflix had previously secured Japanese rights to the event in a deal announced last August.

Both Fox and Netflix are incumbent MLB rights partners and will presumably be at the negotiating table in 2028. There are six total incumbents heading into 2028, with Fox and Netflix joined by NBCUniversal, TNT Sports, Apple and ESPN — the latter of which was the initial English-language broadcast partner for the WBC in 2006 and 2009.

MLB also has a partnership with TelevisaUnivision, which has carried Game 1 of the World Series in each of the past two seasons and this past year shared WBC rights in Mexico with Disney.

The league is also widely expected to at least attempt to bundle its full suite of local rights into a centralized package, presumably drawing streamers to the table who do not currently own rights.

title: Beauden Barrett nears Bristol move as a two-year deal could make him the Gallagher PREM's top earner
article_text:
Beauden Barrett is in advanced talks to sign for Bristol Bears, according to reports on 24 November 2026.

The All Blacks fly-half and full-back just hit 150 test matches for New Zealand in their heavy defeat to England in the Rugby Nations Championship at Allianz Twickenham last weekend.

Read more: When will Beauden Barrett break the All Blacks test cap record?

A deal for Barrett to join Bristol is close to completion, according to the person posting, who says they were told this.

Bristol’s formal offer is with Barrett’s management, and the club are waiting for confirmation, according to Daily Mail. The deal is rumoured to be worth more than £1 million per season for two years, and it could also make him the highest-paid player in the Gallagher PREM.

All Black sabbaticals after a World Cup or early in a World Cup cycle are common with many opting for Japan, the Top 14 in France or Leinster.

The 2015 World Cup winner only has to look to his brother Jordie for the benefits of a sabbatical with the centre having played the 2024-25 season at Leinster, where he was then able to catapult towards some of his best rugby afterwards.

Newcastle Red Bulls have already turned down the chance to sign Barrett, the New Zealander, according to Ruck. Bristol reportedly face competition for Barrett from an unnamed French Top 14 club, according to Ruck.

title: Sinner Issues Update on Knee Surgery
article_text:
Jannik Sinner underwent successful right knee surgery in Finland today—and will require at least three months to recover, Italian media reports.

The 25-year-old Sinner had successful right knee surgery in Turku, Finland today, Dr. Herbert Schönhuber, a sports physician, told Italy’s RaiNews.

Sinner confirmed the surgery with this social media post today.

“After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we’d all hoped, that’s why today I understand a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band,” Sinner said in a post on X. “I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team.

Over the past few months, together with my team we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we’d all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team. Thank you for all your support. See you soon! ❤️ Jannik

Italian journalist Gabriele Parpiglia reported Sinner is suffering from Iliotibial Band Syndrome above his right knee, a condition common in distance runners, Johns Hopkins reports.

Two-time Wimbledon winner Sinner had surgery performed by orthopedic surgeon Dr. Lasse Lempainen, who had examined the Italian superstar last weekend in Milan, according to Italian media.

“As part of the operation, the Finnish specialist lengthened the so-called iliotibial ligament – a strong tendon strip that runs along the outside of the thigh up to the knee,” RaiNews reported today. “According to Herbert Schönhuber, this very method was the most medically gentle and stress-relieving solution to permanently resolve the tennis professional’s persistent complaints.”

Sinner’s expected recovery time is about three months, which means he will almost certainly miss the 2027 Australian Open, which begins in January.

Sinner won the 2024 and 2025 Australian Open titles before bowing to Novak Djokovic at the Melbourne major in January. Carlos Alcaraz defeated Djokovic in the AO final becoming the youngest man in history to complete the career Grand Slam.

Five-time Grand Slam champion Sinner has not played a match since successfully defending his Wimbledon championship with a 6-7(7), 7-6(2), 6-3, 6-4 triumph over Alexander Zverev on Centre Court on July 12th.

Down a set, Sinner snuffed out the second seed’s threat holding in all 22 service games, saving the lone break point he faced and firing 15 aces against only 2 double faults.

Sinner posted a 44-3 record with six tournaments titles in 2026.

Currently ranked No. 2, Sinner is 350 rankings points ahead of ATP Finals champion and world No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz. If Sinner does indeed miss the 2027 Australian Open, he will lose 800 ranking points from the Melbourne major.

title: Machac beats Draxl, Czechia leads Canada in Davis Cup Final 8 quarterfinal
article_text:
Tomas Machac defeated Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 Tuesday to give Czechia an early 1-0 lead over Canada in their Davis Cup Final 8 quarterfinal tie.

Machac, ranked 59th in the world, won a clean first set in which he scored on both of his break points while defending the only one he faced.

Draxl, from Newmarket, Ont., rebounded in the second set. He overcame five aces and fought off four break points while scoring a key break to go up 4-2.

Machac wrested the momentum back in the third set, clinching the match with his fourth break in the deciding game.

Draxl entered the tie ranked 154th in the world but was a big part of Canada's qualifying win over France last month in Quebec City, beating then-No. 32 Arthur Rinderknech.

Tuesday's second singles match in the best-of-three tie features No. 17 Félix Auger-Aliassime of Montreal against No. 14 Jiri Lehecka. Auger-Aliassime and Duncan Chan of Markham, Ont., are scheduled to face Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl in a series-ending doubles match.

title: Badminton: Malaysia banking on quality over quantity in World Tour Finals
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: Small in numbers but strong in quality.

Malaysia may have only two representatives – Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani (pic) in the men’s doubles and Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah in the women’s doubles – at the World Tour Finals in Hangzhou from Dec 9-13, but both combinations have what it takes to challenge for a place on the podium.

The season-ending tournament offers total prize money of US$3.5mil (RM14,404,600). Despite having its smallest contingent for the tournament, Malaysia will be hoping the two pairs can end the country’s wait for a title since the tournament was rebranded as the World Tour Finals in 2018.

Among Sze Fei-Izzuddin’s rivals are world No. 1 pair Kim Won-ho-Seo Seung-jae, former world champions Takuro Hoki-Yugo Kobayashi of Japan, Indonesia’s Fajar Alfian-Shohibul Fikri, England’s Ben Lane-Sean Vendy and Denmark’s Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard.

Hosts China will also have two representatives in reigning world champions Liang Weikeng-Wang Chang and Chen Boyang-Liu Yi.

Sze Fei-Izzuddin, who missed out on a place in last year’s edition, came close to lifting the title in 2024 but lost to Denmark’s Kim Astrup-Anders Skaarup Rasmussen in the final.

Pearly-Thinaah, meanwhile, will be looking to go one better than last year after their campaign ended in the semi-finals.

They will face stiff competition from China’s Liu Sheng-Tan Ning, as well as Japan’s Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto and Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakanishi.

Other qualifiers include Bulgaria’s Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva, Taiwan’s Hsu Yin-hui-Lin Jhih-yun, Indonesia’s Amallia Cahaya-Siti Fadia Ramdhanti and South Korea’s reigning world champions Baek Ha-na-Lee So-hee.

The draw for the Finals will be held on Dec 5.

The eight qualifiers in each event will be divided into two groups, with the top two players or pairs from each group advancing to the semi-finals.

Malaysia’s last title at the season-ending tournament came through Tan Wee Kiong-Goh V Shem, who won the Super Series Finals in Dubai in 2016.

title: 'Very Australian': Smith wants Ripper GC name to LIV on
article_text:
Long-time skipper of the all-Australian Ripper GC team, Cameron Smith has outlined his plans for the popular branding following LIV Golf's demise.

Strident junior golf supporter Cameron Smith hopes the Ripper GC name will live on despite the collapse of LIV Golf.

Captain of the all-Australian outfit for four years, Ripper GC drew huge galleries while winning three team events on the Saudi-backed circuit plus the 2024 season-ending championship.

But while the team is no more after LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy, Smith would love to see the Ripper GC brand endure in some shape or form, likely in a junior development capacity.

The 33-year-old former British Open champ established the Cameron Smith Scholarship in 2016 and also contributes to the broader Australian Golf Foundation.

"I would love it too because I think it's a great name and and it's grown a lot of legs the last few years," Smith said ahead of Thursday's first round of the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney.

"It's very Australian and I think a lot of kids have a lot of great memories with it as well.

"But we don't really know where that stands with everything going on, but for sure I would love to do something."

While the likes of LIV peers Phil Mickelson, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm have polarised during golf's great divide, Smith's reputation as a fan favourite has remained relatively intact.

He proved the Pied Piper of the fairways annually at LIV Golf Adelaide and said he always felt the love of golf galleries around the world and especially at home.

"I've always had great support in Australia," the three-time Australian PGA Championship winner said.

"I'm so thankful for that. (It) was a difficult time for me, so I'm thankful for particularly Adelaide and Australia in general for getting behind me."

His name already etched on the Kirkwood Cup three times, Smith enters this week No.171 in the world after being denied the chance to earn ranking points for years playing in the LIV league.

But after missing six straight cuts at the majors, getting into Sunday contention and finishing seventh at this year's US PGA Championship under new swing coach Claude Harmon had renewed his belief.

"It's been a while since I've been able to perform in a major. I'd just started working with Claude probably two or three weeks before that," Smith said.

"Whenever you make a change, you're really unsure if it was the right decision or not, and that just hit the nail on the head and got the ball rolling and we've been doing the right stuff and the game's felt really good.

"We just need the putts to go in and the results to follow."

title: David Puig’s Ryder Cup Dream Hits A New Road After LIV Collapse
article_text:
David Puig has made his target crystal clear. The 24-year-old Spaniard wants a spot on Europe's 2027 Ryder Cup team. He told reporters that making the squad is "another dream of mine since I was young." This isn't just a side note for the young star. Puig sees the team at Adare Manor next September as his main goal now that the LIV Golf landscape has shifted.

Puig is starting his full season on the DP World Tour this week. He defends his Australian PGA Championship title in Sydney. The field includes major winners like Cameron Smith and Adam Scott. Puig knows the path is steep. In 2026, his world ranking peaked at 56th. A top-20 result was also achieved at the US PGA Championship. But the road to the Ryder Cup requires consistency. "Playing in a Ryder Cup would be amazing," Puig added, according to Golfmagic. "I'll try my best. Hopefully it's enough to be on the team in September."

While Puig chases a player spot, others have already lost their shot at leadership. Ian Poulter confessed he would give up his Ryder Cup captaincy hopes for Europe. He discussed the price he paid after joining the Saudi-backed league. Poulter said he accepted the possibility of losing the role. "Yes, I've sacrificed being a Ryder Cup captain," he said. He understood the rules when he made his move.

The financial hit was real too. The DP World Tour reportedly fined Poulter approximately $1.1 million. The tour confirmed in June 2026 that Poulter settled the debt. That payment did not restore his eligibility for future leadership. The rules state that players who resign their membership cannot become captains. Poulter even compared his earnings to a potential $10 million a year deal with Sky Sports. He described his career earnings as "an obscene amount of money." The message is simple. You cannot play both sides and expect a leadership role.

Puig's situation offers a stark contrast to the LIV fallout. The 24-year-old has not resigned his membership. During the tour's three-week Opening Swing, Puig intends to compete two times. He will skip the Australian Open to play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa. He wants to see more of the world while building his case for Europe. "It's hard when two great tournaments combine with each other," Puig explained. "It was definitely a tough decision, but I'm looking forward to playing here this week and there next week." His focus remains on the game. "But it starts in weeks like this where playing good golf definitely matters."

European captain Luke Donald is seeking a historic third consecutive victory. The team will face the United States at Adare Manor.

title: Marco Penge puts difficult year behind him to secure PGA tour card
article_text:
Marco Penge pulled off one of the most dramatic escapes in recent golf history at the 2026 RSM Classic. Entering the final week of the season ranked 120th in the FedEx Cup standings, the 28-year-old Englishman needed a top-four finish just to keep his PGA Tour card.

He delivered far more, birdieing the 72nd hole to force a four-man playoff before draining a clutch birdie putt on the first extra hole to claim his maiden PGA Tour title and a two-year exemption. Here is the story behind the resilient golfer who appears to thrive when his back is against the wall.

1. An accidental start at the driving range

Born in Crawley, England, in May 1998, Penge discovered golf purely by chance at age five. His mother bought his father, Angelo, a cheap set of clubs for his 40th birthday to help him relax. Angelo took young Marco along to the Pease Pottage driving range, where the boy picked up a club and immediately striped the ball straight down the fairway.

That natural talent led to formal lessons at Mannings Heath Golf Club and eventually a standout amateur career that was highlighted by winning the 2015 Scottish Amateur Stroke Play Championship.

After turning professional in 2017, Penge took the long road to the top. He honed his craft on the third-tier PGA EuroPro Tour, earning his first pro victory at the 2019 Irish Masters.

He then graduated to the Challenge Tour, where his breakthrough arrived in 2023. That season, Penge won twice, including the season-ending Rolex Challenge Tour Grand Final, to top the Order of Merit and secure his promotion to the DP World Tour.

Penge has been refreshingly open about living with ADHD, explaining that the condition can easily cause him to overthink on the course. Rather than viewing it as a limitation, he has worked closely with his team to build strict routines and mental structures that prevent overstimulation.

Penge credits understanding his own mind as a massive factor in his professional success, noting that the golf course is actually where he feels most at ease.

Penge’s career hit a major roadblock in December 2024 when the DP World Tour handed him a three-month suspension and a £2,000 fine for breaching its integrity program.

An investigation revealed he had placed small bets on golf tournaments between 2022 and 2024. Although he never wagered on himself or events he was competing in, the ban sidelined him heading into 2025. Penge owned up to the mistake, attributing it to a misunderstanding of the rules.

Returning from suspension in February 2025, Penge played with a chip on his shoulder and enjoyed a career-defining year. He captured his maiden DP World Tour title at the Hainan Classic in April, followed by victories at the Danish Golf Championship and the Spanish Open.

He finished second in the Race to Dubai rankings, climbed inside the world’s top 30, reportedly turned down a massive LIV Golf offer, and earned his 2026 PGA Tour card.

Penge’s 2026 transition to the United States tested his resilience to the limit. Following a move to Florida with his wife, Sophie, the couple endured a terrifying stretch when their newborn son spent four weeks in neonatal intensive care.

Simultaneously, Penge battled a debilitating viral illness and vertigo that forced him to step away from golf for six weeks after the PGA Championship.

Slumping in the standings, he arrived at Sea Island needing a miracle – but he delivered in style to turn a season of personal and physical adversity into a career-defining triumph.
